# Overview

This file multiply imputes the country-by-year covariates created in `01 - Covariate Cleaning.qmd` (`FPI_GDP_IHMESHOCK_WPP_SDI.csv`). It replaces `Imputation of IHME covariate data_multiple_impute.R`, which used the old SDI, GDP and WPP 2022 data, and uses the same general method. The covariates imputed are:

| Variable | Description | Observed years |
|----|----|----|
| `SDI` | Socio-demographic index (GBD 2023) | through 2023 |
| `fpi_avg` | Food price index (yearly average) | 2001 - 2026 |
| `shock` | IHME shock mortality covariate | through 2023 |
| `war_terror` | IHME war and terror mortality covariate | through 2023 |
| `log_gdp_pc` | Log of GDP per capita (current US$) | through 2025 |
| `dpt_imm` | DPT immunization, % of children 12-23 months (World Bank) | through 2024 |

`fpi_prev5yr_avg` and `fpi_anom` are derived from `fpi_avg`, so they are recomputed from the imputed `fpi_avg` rather than imputed separately. `fpi_max` is not imputed (it is not used downstream). `gdp` (GDP per capita growth, %) and the WPP indicators are only used as predictors; `gdp` is carried through unimputed. GDP per capita (`gdp_pc`, US$) is imputed on the log scale (`log_gdp_pc`) and is also used as a predictor for the other variables; the output has both `log_gdp_pc` and `gdp_pc = exp(log_gdp_pc)`. `dpt_imm` is a percentage imputed on the logit scale and returned as a percentage. It is not used as a predictor for the other variables.

For each variable, the steps are the same as in the old program:

1.  **Country-level means.** Impute the variable (together with GDP and the WPP demographic indicators) with `mice`, and compute each country's mean over the observed years in every imputation.
2.  **Mean-centered imputation.** Mean center the variable by country, reshape to wide format (one column per year) and impute again with `mice`. The imputed variable is the country mean plus the centered value.
3.  **Years after the last observed year.** Fit the penalized longitudinal model (`cmnpe`) to the recent trend and draw the future values from its predictive distribution. This step is skipped if the variable is observed through the last year (`fpi_avg`).

Observed values are always kept as observed. All paths are relative to the repository root.

# Settings

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(mice)
library(parallel)
library(doParallel)
library(slider)
library(this.path)

# knitr resets the working directory after every chunk, so root.dir is needed
# for the whole document (see 01 - Covariate Cleaning.qmd).
repo_dir <- dirname(this.dir())
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_dir)
setwd(repo_dir)
source("Utils/Programs_Oct_2026.R")
```

```{r}
first_year <- 1984   # first year of covariate data
last_year  <- 2026   # last year to impute for
jme_year   <- "2026" # year folder of the JME raw data (only used for the country list)
cov_file   <- "Data/IHME_covs/FPI_GDP_IHMESHOCK_WPP_SDI.csv"  # from 01 - Covariate Cleaning.qmd
out_label  <- "Oct2026" # appended to the output file names (the old files are not overwritten)

# A year is treated as "observed" for a variable if at least this share of the
# countries have data for it. This sets the first and last observed years.
min_obs_share <- 0.5

# Number of imputations (IMP_B can be set to a small number for a quick test run)
B <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("IMP_B", unset = "20"))
seed_base <- 238746
## Settings tried, in order, if the trend model fails (see the imputation function)
retry_grid <- expand_grid(knot_step = c(2, 3), y_scale = c(1, 10, 100, 1000, 1e4, 1e-2, 0.1, 1e5))

## Number of cores: the largest divisor of B that is <= the available cores - 1.
## This keeps n.core * n.imp.core == B (parlmice overrides m otherwise).
max_cores <- max(1, min(B, parallel::detectCores() -2))
n_core <- max(Filter(function(d) B %% d == 0, seq_len(max_cores)))
n_imp_core <- B / n_core

## Runs mice in parallel (forked processes, macOS/Linux): n_core runs of n_imp_core
## imputations each, combined into one mids object with B imputations.
## (parlmice is deprecated and does not work when called inside a function.)
par_mice <- function(data, pred, meth, seed, maxit = 20) {
  runs <- mclapply(
    seq_len(n_core),
    function(i) mice(data, m = n_imp_core, predictorMatrix = pred, method = meth,
                     maxit = maxit, printFlag = FALSE, seed = seed + i),
    mc.cores = n_core, mc.set.seed = FALSE
  )
  if (any(map_lgl(runs, \(r) inherits(r, "try-error")))) stop("mice failed in a worker.")
  reduce(runs, ibind)
}

# WPP indicators used to predict the covariates (the same as the old program)
wpp_vars <- c("PopDensity", "MedianAgePop", "CBR", "TFR",
              "Births1519", "CDR", "LEx", "IMR", "Q5")
```

Each variable is imputed on a scale where it is roughly symmetric: `SDI` is not transformed (it is bounded to [0.001, 1] after imputation, and its trend is modeled on the logit scale, as before), `shock` and `war_terror` are right skewed so `log(x)` is used (the few zeros are first set to the smallest positive value divided by $\sqrt{2}$, see below), and `fpi_avg` has extreme values (hyperinflation) and negative values so `asinh` is used. GDP per capita is right skewed and positive so it is imputed as `log(gdp_pc)` (no transformation back and forth is needed for the trend model). `dpt_imm` (a percentage) is imputed on the logit scale; values of exactly 0 or 100 would not have a logit, so they are moved off the boundary in the same way as the zeros above (there are currently none: the observed range is 1 to 99).

```{r}
## Percentages (0-100) on the logit scale. Zeros and 100s are handled when the data are read in.
logit_pct <- function(x) qlogis(x / 100)
inv_logit_pct <- function(y) 100 * plogis(y)

var_cfg <- list(
  SDI = list(
    col = "sdi",
    to = identity, from = identity,       # scale used for the imputation
    lo = 0.001, hi = 1,                   # valid range on that scale
    to_trend = function(x) qlogis(x / 1.15),   # scale used for the trend model
    from_trend = function(y) 1.15 * plogis(y)
  ),
  shock = list(
    col = "shock",
    to = log, from = exp,
    lo = -Inf, hi = Inf
  ),
  war_terror = list(
    col = "war_terror",
    to = log, from = exp,
    lo = -Inf, hi = Inf
  ),
  fpi_avg = list(
    col = "fpi_avg",
    to = asinh, from = sinh,
    lo = -Inf, hi = Inf
  ),
  log_gdp_pc = list(
    col = "log_gdp_pc",                   # log of GDP per capita (US$), made below
    to = identity, from = identity,
    lo = -Inf, hi = Inf
  ),
  dpt_imm = list(
    col = "dpt_imm",
    to = logit_pct, from = inv_logit_pct,
    lo = -Inf, hi = Inf
  )
)
# The trend model uses the imputation scale unless specified otherwise.
var_cfg <- map(var_cfg, function(cfg) {
  if (is.null(cfg$to_trend)) cfg$to_trend <- cfg$to
  if (is.null(cfg$from_trend)) cfg$from_trend <- cfg$from
  cfg
})
```

# Read in and Merge Data

The country list is the countries in the covariate file (those with an ISO3 code) plus any country in the JME survey data, so every survey country gets covariates.

```{r}
cov_raw <- read_csv(cov_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

cov_dat <- cov_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(country_code), year >= first_year, year <= last_year) |>
  transmute(
    ISO3Code = country_code,
    location_name = coalesce(gbd_location_name, country),
    year, sdi, gdp, gdp_pc, dpt_imm, fpi_avg, shock, war_terror,
    TPopulation1Jan, across(all_of(wpp_vars))
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cov_dat[, c("ISO3Code", "year")]))

## Zeros cannot be log (or logit) transformed. There are few, so rather than adding a
## constant to every value, the zeros are set to the smallest positive value divided
## by sqrt(2). (Percentages at 100 are moved below 100 by the same rule.)
## This applies to the observed values too, so the zeros are also replaced in the output.
fix_zeros <- function(x, name) {
  n0 <- sum(x <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n0 > 0) {
    m <- min(x[x > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
    message(name, ": ", n0, " zero value(s) set to ", signif(m / sqrt(2), 4))
    x[!is.na(x) & x <= 0] <- m / sqrt(2)
  }
  x
}
fix_pct <- function(x, name) {
  x <- fix_zeros(x, name)
  n100 <- sum(x >= 100, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n100 > 0) {
    u <- max(x[x < 100], na.rm = TRUE)
    message(name, ": ", n100, " value(s) of 100 set to ", signif(100 - (100 - u) / sqrt(2), 4))
    x[!is.na(x) & x >= 100] <- 100 - (100 - u) / sqrt(2)
  }
  x
}

cov_dat <- cov_dat |>
  mutate(
    shock = fix_zeros(shock, "shock"),
    war_terror = fix_zeros(war_terror, "war_terror"),
    dpt_imm = fix_pct(dpt_imm, "dpt_imm")
  )

## Countries in the JME survey data
jme_files <- list.files(
  paste0("Data/JME/", jme_year, "/Raw"),
  pattern = "^JME_Country_Level_Input_.*\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE
)
if (length(jme_files) == 0) {
  stop("No JME files found in Data/JME/", jme_year, "/Raw. Update `jme_year`.")
}
jme_countries <- map_dfr(jme_files, \(f) read_excel(f) |> distinct(ISO3Code, Country)) |>
  distinct(ISO3Code, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(ISO3Code))

All_countries <- full_join(
  jme_countries,
  cov_dat |> distinct(ISO3Code, location_name),
  by = "ISO3Code"
) |>
  mutate(location_name = coalesce(location_name, Country)) |>
  select(ISO3Code, location_name)

# JME countries with no covariate data (these are imputed from the year trend only)
setdiff(jme_countries$ISO3Code, cov_dat$ISO3Code)
```

A complete country-by-year grid is used so that every country has a row for every year.

```{r}
all_cov <- expand_grid(
  ISO3Code = All_countries$ISO3Code,
  year = first_year:last_year
) |>
  left_join(All_countries, by = "ISO3Code") |>
  left_join(cov_dat |> select(-location_name), by = c("ISO3Code", "year")) |>
  mutate(lpop = log(TPopulation1Jan),
         log_gdp_pc = log(gdp_pc)) |>
  select(ISO3Code, location_name, year, sdi, fpi_avg, shock, war_terror,
         gdp, log_gdp_pc, dpt_imm, lpop, all_of(wpp_vars))

stopifnot(!anyNA(all_cov$year), !anyDuplicated(all_cov[, c("ISO3Code", "year")]))

# Number of distinct countries
n_distinct(all_cov$ISO3Code)
```

## Observed years for each variable

```{r}
windows <- map(var_cfg, function(cfg) {
  yrs <- all_cov |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(share = mean(!is.na(.data[[cfg$col]]))) |>
    filter(share >= min_obs_share) |>
    pull(year)
  c(start = min(yrs), end = max(yrs))
})
bind_rows(windows, .id = "variable")
```

Years before `start` have no data for any country and stay missing. Years after `end` are predicted with the trend model (Section 5).

# Imputation function

```{r}
impute_covariate <- function(name, k) {
  cfg <- var_cfg[[name]]
  col <- cfg$col
  start <- windows[[name]][["start"]]
  end <- windows[[name]][["end"]]
  message("==== Imputing ", name, " (observed ", start, "-", end, ") ====")

  dat <- all_cov |>
    filter(year >= start) |>
    # GDP growth and log GDP per capita are predictors for the other variables
    select(ISO3Code, location_name, year, all_of(col), gdp, any_of("log_gdp_pc"),
           lpop, all_of(wpp_vars))

  ### Step 1. Imputation to create country-level means by imputation ###
  ## The first two columns are IDs and are not used as predictors.
  ini <- mice(dat, maxit = 0)
  pred <- ini$pred
  meth <- ini$method
  pred[, 1:2] <- 0
  diag(pred) <- 0

  imp <- par_mice(dat, pred, meth, seed = seed_base + 100 * k)

  imp_long <- mice::complete(imp, action = "long") |> as_tibble()

  # Country mean (on the imputation scale) over the observed years
  country_mean <- imp_long |>
    filter(year <= end) |>
    mutate(v = cfg$to(.data[[col]])) |>
    group_by(.imp, ISO3Code) |>
    summarise(mn = mean(v), .groups = "drop")

  # Imputed log population (needed for the trend model)
  lpop_imp <- imp_long |> select(.imp, ISO3Code, year, lpop)

  ### Step 2. Imputation on mean centered data (wide format) ###
  wide <- dat |>
    filter(year <= end) |>
    mutate(v = cfg$to(.data[[col]])) |>
    group_by(ISO3Code) |>
    mutate(Z = v - mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(Z = if_else(is.nan(Z), NA_real_, Z)) |>
    select(ISO3Code, year, Z) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = Z, names_prefix = "Z_")

  # Years with very few observations cannot be imputed in the wide format
  z_obs <- colSums(!is.na(wide[, -1]))
  if (any(z_obs < 5)) {
    warning(name, ": years with < 5 observations dropped from the wide imputation: ",
            paste(names(z_obs)[z_obs < 5], collapse = ", "))
    wide <- wide |> select(ISO3Code, all_of(names(z_obs)[z_obs >= 5]))
  }

  ini <- mice(wide, maxit = 0)
  pred <- ini$pred
  pred[1, ] <- 0
  pred[, 1] <- 0
  imp_z <- par_mice(wide, pred, ini$method, seed = seed_base + 100 * k + 50)

  z_long <- mice::complete(imp_z, action = "long") |>
    as_tibble() |>
    pivot_longer(
      starts_with("Z_"), names_prefix = "Z_",
      names_to = "year", names_transform = list(year = as.numeric),
      values_to = "Z"
    )

  ### Reconstruct the variable: country mean + centered value ###
  recon <- z_long |>
    left_join(country_mean, by = c(".imp", "ISO3Code")) |>
    mutate(imp_c = mn + Z)
  ## The additive reconstruction can fall outside the valid range, so values are clamped.
  n_clamped <- sum(!is.na(recon$imp_c) & (recon$imp_c < cfg$lo | recon$imp_c > cfg$hi))
  message(name, ": ", n_clamped, " imputed values were outside [", cfg$lo, ", ",
          cfg$hi, "] and were clamped.")

  recon <- recon |>
    mutate(imp_raw = cfg$from(pmin(pmax(imp_c, cfg$lo), cfg$hi))) |>
    select(.imp, ISO3Code, year, imp_raw) |>
    # Observed values are kept as observed
    left_join(dat |> select(ISO3Code, year, obs = all_of(col)),
              by = c("ISO3Code", "year")) |>
    mutate(imp_raw = coalesce(obs, imp_raw)) |>
    select(-obs)

  if (anyNA(recon$imp_raw)) {
    stop(name, ": missing imputed values up to ", end, " (check the wide imputation).")
  }

  ### Step 3. Years after the last observed year ###
  out <- expand_grid(.imp = 1:B, ISO3Code = All_countries$ISO3Code,
                     year = start:last_year) |>
    left_join(recon, by = c(".imp", "ISO3Code", "year"))

  if (end < last_year) {
    trend_start <- max(start, end - 9)
    P_all_data <- out |>
      left_join(lpop_imp, by = c(".imp", "ISO3Code", "year")) |>
      mutate(country = ISO3Code,
             Y = cfg$to_trend(imp_raw),   # NA after the last observed year
             SE_var = 1)

    registerDoParallel(cores = n_core)
    fits <- foreach(j = 1:B, .packages = c("tidyverse", "nlme", "splines", "Matrix")) %dopar% {
      source("Utils/Programs_Oct_2026.R")
      all_data <- P_all_data |> filter(.imp == j & year >= trend_start)
      data_w_out <- all_data |> select(country, year, Y, SE_var)
      data_w_out$SE_pred <- data_w_out$SE_var

      DF_R <- quantile(data_w_out$year, probs = c(0.5))
      B.knots <- range(data_w_out$year[!is.na(data_w_out$Y)])
      B.knots[1] <- B.knots[1] - 1
      B.knots[2] <- B.knots[2] + 10
      DF_P <- seq(min(data_w_out$year), end, 2)
      # cmnpe needs a covariate called "Sex"; log population is used here
      cov_data <- cbind(Sex = all_data$lpop, lpop2 = all_data$lpop^2)

      ## The fit occasionally fails with "Inverse failed" for a particular imputation:
      ## SDI-like series are so smooth that the estimated variances are tiny and the
      ## variance matrices become numerically singular, and whether a fit succeeds
      ## is sensitive to the scale of Y. If a fit fails, it is retried with Y
      ## multiplied by other constants (the model is scale invariant, so the
      ## predictions and SDs are divided by the constant afterwards) and then with
      ## a wider knot spacing for the penalized spline.
      Y_orig <- data_w_out$Y
      Estimation <- NULL
      for (attempt in seq_len(nrow(retry_grid))) {
        y_scale <- retry_grid$y_scale[attempt]
        data_w_out$Y <- Y_orig * y_scale
        DF_P_try <- seq(min(data_w_out$year), end, retry_grid$knot_step[attempt])
        fit <- try(capture.output(
          Estimation <- cmnpe(data_w_out, DF_P_try, DF_R, B.knots, q.order = 2,
                              cov_data = cov_data, Pcov_data = NULL,
                              cov_mat = "VC", plots = FALSE, TRANS = FALSE,
                              zero_covs = NULL, slope = TRUE)
        ), silent = TRUE)
        if (!inherits(fit, "try-error")) break
      }
      if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) stop(name, ": trend model failed for imputation ", j)
      pd <- Estimation$plot_data
      pd$pred <- pd$pred / y_scale
      pd$sigma_Y_est <- pd$sigma_Y_est / y_scale
      pd$attempts <- attempt - 1
      pd
    }
    stopImplicitCluster()
    n_retry <- sum(map_dbl(fits, \(f) f$attempts[1]) > 0)
    message(name, ": the trend model needed a refit for ", n_retry, " of ", B, " imputations.")

    ## Draw the values after the last observed year from the predictive distribution.
    ## One standard normal draw is used per country and imputation (scaled by the
    ## predictive SD of each year) so the draws are not independent noise from year
    ## to year.
    draws <- map_dfr(1:B, function(j) {
      set.seed(seed_base + 1000 * k + j)
      fits[[j]] |>
        as_tibble() |>
        mutate(.imp = j, ISO3Code = as.character(country)) |>
        filter(year > end) |>
        group_by(ISO3Code, year) |>
        filter(row_number() == 1) |>
        ungroup() |>
        arrange(ISO3Code, year) |>
        select(.imp, ISO3Code, year, pred, sigma_Y_est) |>
        group_by(ISO3Code) |>
        mutate(z_draw = rnorm(1)) |>
        ungroup() |>
        mutate(draw_raw = cfg$from_trend(pred + z_draw * sigma_Y_est)) |>
        select(.imp, ISO3Code, year, draw_raw)
    })

    out <- out |>
      left_join(draws, by = c(".imp", "ISO3Code", "year")) |>
      mutate(imp_raw = if_else(year > end, draw_raw, imp_raw)) |>
      select(-draw_raw)
  }

  if (anyNA(out$imp_raw)) {
    stop(name, ": missing imputed values remain (check the trend model output).")
  }

  out |> rename(!!name := imp_raw)
}
```

# Run the imputations

Each variable takes a few minutes (two `mice` runs per variable, plus the trend model for `SDI`, `shock` and `war_terror`).

```{r}
imputed <- map2(names(var_cfg), seq_along(var_cfg), impute_covariate) |>
  set_names(names(var_cfg))
```

## Checking the imputed values

Ranges of the imputed variables, and trajectories (one line per imputation) for a sample of countries:

```{r}
imputed |>
  imap_dfr(\(d, nm) summarise(d, variable = nm, min = min(.data[[nm]]),
                              median = median(.data[[nm]]), max = max(.data[[nm]]))) |>
  as.data.frame()

set.seed(seed_base+1)
samp_iso <- sample(unique(all_cov$ISO3Code), 25)
for (nm in names(imputed)) {
  p <- imputed[[nm]] |>
    filter(ISO3Code %in% samp_iso) |>
    left_join(All_countries, by = "ISO3Code") |>
    ggplot(aes(x = year, y = .data[[nm]], group = .imp)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = windows[[nm]][["end"]], linetype = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~location_name) +
    labs(title = nm, caption = "Dashed line: last observed year")
  print(p)
}
```

# Final variables

`fpi_prev5yr_avg` and `fpi_anom` are recomputed from the imputed `fpi_avg`, in the same way as in `01 - Covariate Cleaning.qmd` (the mean of the 5 previous years, which needs a complete 5 years of history).

```{r}
all_imp <- expand_grid(.imp = 1:B, ISO3Code = All_countries$ISO3Code,
                       year = first_year:last_year) |>
  left_join(All_countries, by = "ISO3Code") |>
  left_join(all_cov |> select(ISO3Code, year, gdp), by = c("ISO3Code", "year")) |>
  reduce(imputed, \(acc, d) left_join(acc, d, by = c(".imp", "ISO3Code", "year")),
         .init = _) |>
  arrange(.imp, ISO3Code, year) |>
  group_by(.imp, ISO3Code) |>
  mutate(
    gdp_pc = exp(log_gdp_pc),
    fpi_prev5yr_avg = slide_dbl(fpi_avg, mean, .before = 5, .after = -1,
                                .complete = TRUE),
    fpi_anom = fpi_avg - fpi_prev5yr_avg
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(.imp, ISO3Code, year, location_name, SDI, gdp, log_gdp_pc, gdp_pc, dpt_imm,
         fpi_avg, fpi_prev5yr_avg, fpi_anom, shock, war_terror)

# Missing values by variable and year range (fpi is not available before 2001 by design)
all_imp |>
  filter(year > 1989) |>
  mutate(period = if_else(year < 2001, "1990-2000", "2001-2026")) |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(across(c(SDI, gdp, log_gdp_pc, gdp_pc, dpt_imm, fpi_avg,
                     fpi_prev5yr_avg, fpi_anom, shock, war_terror),
                   \(x) sum(is.na(x))))

save(all_cov, imputed, windows, all_imp,
     file = paste0("Data/IHME_covs/Imputation_", out_label, ".RData"))
```

## Merge with the region and income group data and save

The data is created for all three sexes (the covariates do not vary by sex), as in the old program.

```{r}
cov_data <- readRDS("Data/IHME_covs/Tidy_World_Devel_Indic.rds")

all_cov_long <- all_imp |>
  mutate(Sex = "Both") |>
  bind_rows(all_imp |> mutate(Sex = "Male")) |>
  bind_rows(all_imp |> mutate(Sex = "Female")) |>
  arrange(ISO3Code, year, Sex)

## One name per country. Tidy_World_Devel_Indic.rds only goes to 2023, and its
## names can differ from the imputed data's (e.g. "Turkey" vs "Türkiye", "Nauru"
## vs "Naoero"). Taking the name row by row gave a different name for 2024-2026,
## and since the model identifies countries by name, those years became a
## separate country with no data. Use the Tidy name (it matches the JME survey
## data) if the country has one, otherwise the imputed data's name.
P_cov_data <- cov_data |>
  full_join(all_cov_long, by = c("ISO.code" = "ISO3Code", "year", "Sex")) |>
  group_by(ISO.code) |>
  mutate(location_name = coalesce(
    first(na.omit(location_name.x)),
    first(na.omit(location_name.y)),
    first(na.omit(as.character(Country)))
  )) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-c("location_name.x", "location_name.y"))

# Should be zero rows (one name per country)
P_cov_data |> distinct(ISO.code, location_name) |> count(ISO.code) |> filter(n > 1)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(distinct(P_cov_data, ISO.code, location_name)$ISO.code))

cov_data <- P_cov_data |>
  arrange(.imp, ISO.code, Sex, year) |>
  filter(year > 1989) |>
  group_by(.imp, ISO.code, Sex) |>
  fill(Region:Country) |>
  ungroup()

# Should be zero rows
cov_data |> count(.imp, ISO.code, Sex, year) |> filter(n > 1)
```

```{r}
saveRDS(cov_data, paste0("Data/IHME_covs/Multiple_Imputed_", out_label, ".rds"))

### Single imputation file: the average over the imputations of every numeric
### variable (NA if all are missing). Non-numeric variables (e.g., Region, Country,
### income group) are carried over.
mean_na <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}
cov_data_mean <- cov_data |>
  group_by(ISO.code, Sex, year) |>
  summarise(
    across(where(is.numeric) & !any_of(".imp"), mean_na),
    across(!where(is.numeric), first),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

saveRDS(cov_data_mean, paste0("Data/IHME_covs/Single_Impute_", out_label, ".rds"))
```

The downstream program `2 - Preparing Primary Data/3 - Merging Survey_Covariate_Data.R` reads `Multiple_Imputed_Oct2026.rds` and `Single_Impute_Oct2026.rds` (set by `imputed_label` there).
